First, we pull out the factor of $4$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{x+1}{4(x+\frac{1}{4})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{4})}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{1}{4} & 1 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{1}{4} \\  & 1 & \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{4})} & =1+\frac{(\frac{3}{4})}{(x+\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =1+\frac{3}{4(x+\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =1+\frac{3}{4x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}\int (1+\frac{3}{4x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\int \text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{4x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[x+\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+1|]+C \\  & =\frac{x}{4}+\frac{3}{16}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$
